title: Trilce: Poem XIX - To Rummage, Sweet Helpide, You Clear
text:
To rummage, sweet Helpide, you clear,

how we remain from so much remaining.


Today you come when I have barely risen.

The stable is divinely pissed

and excremented by the innocent cow

and the innocent ass and the innocent rooster.


Enter the ecumenical Mary.

O saintgabriel, make the soul conceive,

the lightless love, the skyless one,

the most stone, the most nothing,

                   even the monarch illusion.


We will burn all the ships!

We will burn the final essence!


But if one must suffer from myth to myth,

and you arrive to speak to me chewing ice,

let us chew embers;

there is nowhere left to descend,

there is nowhere left to climb.


The rooster has turned uncertain, man.
editorial_note: The translation keeps Vallejo's irreverent stable imagery, saintgabriel neologism, and final uncertain rooster.

title: Trilce: Poem LIX - The Terrestrial Sphere of Love
text:
The terrestrial sphere of love,

which lagged behind below, turns

and turns without stopping a second,

and we are condemned to suffer

its spinning like a center.


Pacific motionless, glass, pregnant

with all possibles.

Cold Andes, inhumanable, pure.

Perhaps. Perhaps.


The sphere turns in the flint of time,

and sharpens itself,

and sharpens itself until it wants to lose itself;

it turns, forging before the deserted flanks

that point so frightfully known,

because it has gestated, turn

after turn,

the familiar little corral.


Centrifugal yes, yes,

yes,

yes, yes, yes, yes: NO!

And I withdraw until I blue, and withdrawing

I harden, until I press my soul tight!
editorial_note: The translation preserves the rotating love-sphere, repeated yeses, abrupt NO, and the invented verb 'to blue.'

title: Trilce: Poem XLVIII - I Now Have 70 Peruvian Soles
text:
I now have 70 Peruvian soles.

I take the next-to-last coin, the one that rings

69 Punic times.

And here it is, at the end of its role,

burning itself all over and blazing,

                                                    blazing,

round between my hallucinated eardrums.


It, being 69, strikes against 70;

then climbs 71, rebounds on 72.

And so it multiplies and mirrors itself undaunted

in all the other pinions.


It, vibrating and struggling,

letting out shouuutss,

releasing arduous, crackling silences,

pissing itself with natural greatness,

in unanimous rising posts,

ends up being all the numerals,

                                                the whole of life.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the coin's arithmetic hallucination, repeated blazing, stretched shout, and bodily comedy.

title: Willow
text:
Winter lyricism, murmur of crapes,

        when the swift departure already draws near;

        ominous voices of sad songs

        that in the afternoon pray a farewell.


        Vision of the burial of my illusions

        in the very tomb of a mortal wound.

        Veronica charity of unknown regions,

        where life is lost at the price of ether.


        Near dawn I will leave weeping;

        and as my years go on bending,

        my swift road will bend scythes.


        And before cold oils of a dying moon,

        with tones of steel on indolent earth,

        the dogs will dig, howling, a goodbye!
editorial_note: The translation keeps the early elegiac tone of departure, crape, scythes, dogs, and farewell.

title: Trilce: Poem XXX - Burn of the Second
text:
Burn of the second

on the whole tender little head of desire,

sting of wandering chili pepper,

at two in the immoral afternoon.


Glove of the edges, edge to edge.

Fragrant truth touched live, when connecting

the antenna of sex

with what we are being without knowing it.


Washwater of maximum ablution.

Traveling boilers

that collide and splash fresh shadow

unanimous, the color, the fraction, hard life,

                           hard eternal life.

Let us not fear. Death is like this.


The sex, blood of the beloved, which complains,

sweetened, of bearing so much

for so ridiculous a point.

And the circuit

between our poor day and the great night,

at two in the immoral afternoon.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the erotic circuit, technical vocabulary, and repeated immoral afternoon.
